title: Review: Electrolysis; Exothermic and endothermic reactions
source: Questions and terms copied unchanged from the site's bank for AQA GCSE Chemistry (8462) (review status in the bank: authored-gated-unreviewed). Terms: 4.5.1-c06, 4.4.3-c11, 4.5.1-c07, 4.4.3-c16. Clues: 4.5.1-c06 first sentence of the bank's definition; 4.4.3-c11 first sentence of the bank's definition; 4.5.1-c07 first sentence of the bank's definition; 4.4.3-c16 first sentence of the bank's definition. Questions: 4.5.1-q13, 4.5.1-q14, 4.5.1-q15, 4.4.3-q05, 4.4.3-q15, 4.5.1-q12, 4.4.3-q20, 4.5.1-q11, 4.4.3-q21, 4.5.1-q01, 4.4.3-q14, 4.5.1-q02, 4.4.3-q26, 4.4.3-q27, 4.4.3-q28. The matching task revisits terms from the worlds it reviews, in a new mix. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Oxidation
items.clue: A reaction in which a substance gains oxygen.

items.label: Cryolite
items.clue: The compound mixed with aluminium oxide in the aluminium cell.

items.label: Neutralisation
items.clue: The reaction of an acid with a base or alkali to form a salt and water.

items.label: Hypothesis
items.clue: A testable idea, put forward before the experiment, that predicts what will happen and can be supported or disproved by the results of Required practical 3.

questions.stem: A self-heating can warms coffee using the reaction of calcium oxide with water. Which property makes this reaction suitable for that use?

options.text: It is endothermic, so it draws energy out of the air and into the drink.
It is exothermic, so the reacting chemicals themselves become hotter.
It is exothermic, but only when the temperature change is large.
It is exothermic, so it transfers enough energy to warm the drink in the can.

questions.explanation: An everyday use of an exothermic reaction: energy released by the reaction passes into the drink and raises its temperature.

questions.stem: In Required practical 4 a student adds different volumes of sodium hydroxide to 25 cm3 of acid and records the highest temperature reached. What is the independent variable?

options.text: the volume of sodium hydroxide added
the highest temperature that is reached
the temperature of the acid before mixing
the insulation of the plastic cup

questions.explanation: It is the variable the student deliberately chooses and changes; the highest temperature is what is measured as a result.

questions.stem: Why is the reacting mixture in Required practical 4 placed in a polystyrene cup with a lid?

options.text: to make the reaction happen faster inside the insulated cup
to reduce the energy transferred to and from the surroundings
to make the reaction go faster so that a change can be seen sooner
to stop the temperature of the room from changing at all

questions.explanation: Polystyrene insulates and the lid limits evaporation, so more of the energy change shows up as a temperature change in the mixture.

questions.stem: Molten lead bromide is electrolysed using inert electrodes. What is produced at the cathode?

options.text: Bromine, because the non-metals form there
Lead, the metal, collects at the cathode
Hydrogen, made from water in this melt
Lead ions, Pb²⁺, coating the whole electrode

questions.explanation: Lead ions are positive, so they move to the negative electrode and are discharged as lead metal.

questions.stem: Copper chloride solution is electrolysed with inert electrodes. What forms at the cathode?

options.text: Hydrogen, because copper is less reactive than it
Copper, as it is less reactive than hydrogen
Chlorine, since chloride ions are drawn there
Oxygen, released as the water breaks apart

questions.explanation: The less reactive element is discharged, and copper is below hydrogen in reactivity.

questions.stem: A sports injury pack and a hand warmer each rely on a chemical reaction. Which comparison is correct?

options.text: The injury pack is exothermic; the hand warmer is endothermic.
The injury pack is endothermic and the warmer exothermic.
Both are exothermic, but the injury pack releases energy slowly.
Both are endothermic, and each takes energy from the skin.

questions.explanation: The pack must take energy in from the surroundings to cool a swelling, while the warmer must transfer energy out to the hands.

questions.stem: A student plans Required practical 3 and writes an idea down before starting. Which statement is a hypothesis the investigation could test?

options.text: Copper chloride solution is a clear blue liquid
Bubbles appeared at the negative electrode
Solutions of halides will give a halogen at the anode
Which gas is given off at the negative electrode?

questions.explanation: It is a testable prediction, made in advance, that the results of the practical can support or disprove.

questions.stem: During a neutralisation the thermometer in the mixture rises by 8 °C. What has happened to the energy?

options.text: It has been transferred from the chemicals to the surroundings.
It has been transferred from the surroundings and into the chemicals.
The chemicals still hold the very same energy they had before.
It has been stored in the salt and the water that are made.

questions.explanation: The solution is part of the surroundings, so a rise in its temperature shows energy leaving the chemicals: an exothermic reaction.

questions.stem: In Required practical 3, the gas collected at the cathode gave a squeaky pop with a lit splint. What does this show?

options.text: Hydrogen formed, so the metal is more reactive
Oxygen formed, because oxygen relights the splint
Chlorine formed, since it bleaches damp litmus paper
The metal itself formed and burned with the lit splint

questions.explanation: A squeaky pop identifies hydrogen, which is discharged when the metal is more reactive than hydrogen.

questions.stem: A reaction transfers energy to the surroundings. What must be true of the product molecules?

options.text: They have less energy than the reactants, by the amount transferred out.
They have more energy than the reactants, by the amount given out.
They have less energy, and the energy released no longer exists.
They have exactly the same total energy as the reactants did.

questions.explanation: This is the specification's own statement: the energy that reached the surroundings came from the chemicals, so the products sit lower by exactly that amount.

questions.stem: When an aqueous solution is electrolysed with inert electrodes, what decides which ions are discharged?

options.text: The size of the charge carried by each of the ions
The mass of each of the ions present in the solution
The metal is discharged whatever else is there
The relative reactivity of the elements involved

questions.explanation: The specification states that the ions discharged depend on the relative reactivity of the elements involved.

questions.stem: Which statement about energy during a chemical reaction is correct?

options.text: No energy is transferred to or from the surroundings at all.
The total energy in the universe is the same after the reaction as before.
Some of the energy is destroyed as the surroundings are being warmed.
Reactants and products always contain exactly equal energy.

questions.explanation: Energy is conserved in chemical reactions; the reaction only moves energy between the chemicals and their surroundings.

questions.stem: Which half equation shows hydroxide ions being discharged at the anode?

options.text: 4OH⁻ → 2O₂ + 2H₂O + 4e⁻
2OH⁻ + 2e⁻ → O₂ + H₂O
OH⁻ → O₂ + H₂O + e⁻
4OH⁻ → O₂ + 2H₂O + 4e⁻

questions.explanation: Four hydroxide ions lose four electrons, giving one molecule of oxygen and two of water; atoms and charge balance.

questions.stem: The anode reaction may be written as 4OH⁻ → O₂ + 2H₂O + 4e⁻ or as 4OH⁻ – 4e⁻ → O₂ + 2H₂O. How are the two related?

options.text: The second one supplies electrons instead of removing them
The first is the anode one, the second the cathode one
They are the same reaction, written in two ways
The second one applies to a molten compound only

questions.explanation: Losing four electrons can be shown by subtracting them on the left or adding them on the right.

questions.stem: Complete and balance the half equation for the reaction at the cathode in the aluminium cell.

options.text: 3Al³⁺ + 3e⁻ → 3Al
Al³⁺ + 3e⁻ → Al
Al³⁺ + 3e⁻ → 3Al
Al³⁺ + e⁻ → Al

questions.explanation: Each aluminium ion carries three positive charges, so it gains three electrons to form an aluminium atom.
